subject: physical-education
title: Launch and diagnostic: safety responsibility toward yourself and others
focus: safety responsibility toward yourself and others
essentialQuestion: What makes an activity one that people actually want to come back to?
privacySafeScenario: Redesign a standard activity so that three people with different mobility, experience, and confidence profiles can all participate meaningfully in the same game, and defend each design choice.
studentTask: Learner applies safety responsibility toward yourself and others in a new situation at a self-set intensity and records what they did, noticed, and would adjust.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, explain the key idea behind safety responsibility toward yourself and others and name one adjustment for the next session.
completionCriteria: The learner completes or fully describes the safety responsibility toward yourself and others task using a version their body and setting allow.
The learner gives a cue, principle, tactic, or documented process rather than an unexplained result.
The learner self-assesses against the stated criteria and identifies one next adjustment.
adaptationChoices: The redesign may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically. Practical trial is optional.
extensionChallenge: Apply safety responsibility toward yourself and others under a new constraint, in a different activity, or teach the cue to someone else — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
The redesign may be written, diagrammed, described aloud, or trialed practically. Practical trial is optional.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice or try one safe, optional example of safety responsibility toward yourself and others in daily life. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
